channel.title: IT Threat Intel - IT Cybersecurity
channel.description: Curated IT / enterprise cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] On-prem SharePoint RCE lands in CISA KEV with a federal deadline of today — and it's already tied to Warlock ransomware
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-45659, a remote-code-execution flaw in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server (CVSS 8.8, caused by deserialization of untrusted data), to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 1 July after confirming active exploitation, with a federal remediation deadline of today, 4 July. The bug lets an authenticated user holding only Site Member permissions run code on the server — and notably Microsoft rated exploitation “less likely” when it shipped the fix in May 2026, so any organization that deprioritized it on that basis should re-rank it now. On-prem SharePoint is a workhorse intranet and document store across enterprises, and Storm-2603 — the actor behind Warlock ransomware — has been exploiting on-prem SharePoint since mid-2025, making this a ransomware precursor rather than a theoretical risk. Apply the May 2026 SharePoint update immediately, restrict and monitor authenticated access, and hunt every internet-reachable farm for web shells and anomalous SharePoint process activity. - CISA KEV / BleepingComputer - KEV-added 1 Jul 2026 — federal deadline today, 4 Jul 2026; exploitation ongoing

item.title: [High] Foxconn's North America factories hit — Nitrogen ransomware claims 8TB and 11M+ files exfiltrated
item.description: Some of Foxconn's North America factories suffered a cyberattack, and the Nitrogen ransomware group claimed credit on its leak site, asserting it had exfiltrated more than 11 million files — roughly 8TB of data. The incident lands as fresh data shows manufacturing is the most-targeted ransomware sector by a wide margin, underscoring that plant IT (ERP, file shares, engineering data) is squarely in extortion crews' sights. Manufacturers should validate backups and segmentation, review data-exfiltration monitoring, and confirm incident-response and negotiation playbooks are ready. - Dark Reading - Reported early Jul 2026 — Nitrogen leak-site claim

item.title: [High] Oracle E-Business Suite breach wave widens — University of Phoenix and Cox Enterprises disclose data theft
item.description: The extortion campaign against Oracle E-Business Suite continues to produce named victims: both the University of Phoenix and Cox Enterprises have disclosed data breaches stemming from Oracle EBS hacks. EBS is a core ERP platform holding HR, finance and supplier data, so a single exposed instance can translate into large-scale data theft and extortion. With a fresh unauthenticated EBS takeover flaw now also under active exploitation (see Critical Advisories), organizations running EBS should treat both the patch backlog and breach-notification exposure as urgent. - BleepingComputer - Disclosures reported late Jun–early Jul 2026

item.title: [High] “FortiBleed”: attackers monetize a foothold in thousands of Fortinet firewalls — and add a Nextcloud zero-day
item.description: After gaining a foothold in thousands of Fortinet firewalls, attackers have started to monetize that access — and are piling on a Nextcloud zero-day to extend their reach, according to Dark Reading's reporting on the campaign dubbed “FortiBleed.” Perimeter firewalls are a high-value pivot: a compromised edge device can expose internal networks, VPN sessions and management planes. Organizations running affected Fortinet appliances should verify they are on fixed firmware, hunt for signs of prior compromise (rogue admins, config changes, unexpected tunnels), and rotate credentials and certificates that a foothold could have exposed. - Dark Reading - Reported early Jul 2026 — ongoing monetization

item.title: [High] Sysdig documents “JADEPUFFER” — the first extortion attack run end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent
item.description: Sysdig's Threat Research Team described what it assesses as the first extortion operation executed end-to-end by an AI agent with no human at the keyboard. The actor, JADEPUFFER, gained initial access by exploiting CVE-2025-3248 — a previously KEV-listed remote-code-execution flaw in the Langflow AI-workflow platform — on an internet-facing instance, then autonomously performed reconnaissance, stole credentials, established persistence, compromised a production database and destroyed data before demanding payment. It follows Sysdig's earlier case where an LLM agent chained a CVE through several internal pivots to exfiltrate a full database in under an hour. The tempo is the story: eliminate internet exposure of unpatched apps (especially anything with a KEV-listed CVE), vault and rotate credentials, restrict egress, and tune detection for machine-speed lateral movement. - Sysdig TRT / The Hacker News - Reported 2–3 Jul 2026

item.title: [Medium] Feuding ransomware groups leak each other's data — KryBit hits rival 0APT
item.description: In a sign of just how crowded and unstable the extortion ecosystem has become, ransomware crews are now turning on each other. After being leaked itself, KryBit breached and exfiltrated rival group 0APT's infrastructure, listed 0APT as a victim on its own leak site, and left a taunt: “Next time, don't play with the big boys.” For defenders the practical takeaway is indirect but real — infighting occasionally dumps stolen victim data into the open, and the churn of brands complicates attribution and threat tracking. - Dark Reading - Reported late Jun–early Jul 2026

item.title: [Medium] SANS ISC flags a MetaMask phishing campaign — crypto-wallet lures aimed at end users
item.description: The SANS Internet Storm Center's 1 July handler diary dissected an interesting phishing email targeting MetaMask, the popular cryptocurrency wallet. Wallet-theft phishing continues to be a low-cost, high-reward lure, and it increasingly reaches corporate inboxes as employees mix personal crypto activity with work devices. Refresh phishing awareness for finance and crypto-adjacent staff, reinforce that legitimate wallet providers never ask for seed phrases, and ensure mail filtering and reporting workflows are catching credential- and seed-phrase-harvesting lures. - SANS Internet Storm Center - Handler diary — 1 Jul 2026

item.title: [Critical] Oracle E-Business Suite unauthenticated takeover flaw now exploited — ~950 instances exposed online
item.description: CVE-2026-46817 (CVSS 9.8) is a flaw in the File Transmission component of Oracle Payments within E-Business Suite that lets an unauthenticated attacker with HTTP access take over vulnerable systems through a low-complexity attack. Researchers (Defused) reported the first exploitation attempts against EBS honeypots over the weekend, and Shadowserver tracks roughly 950 EBS instances exposed online — with about 450 confirmed and nearly 200 each in the U.S. and Europe. Oracle addressed the issue in its May 2026 Critical Patch Update. Apply the May CPU immediately, remove internet exposure of EBS, and hunt for signs of takeover given active in-the-wild attempts. - BleepingComputer / Shadowserver - Exploitation reported late Jun–early Jul 2026

item.title: [Critical] Progress Kemp LoadMaster pre-auth RCE now seeing exploitation attempts — the load balancer fronting many enterprise services
item.description: eSentire's Threat Response Unit reported that CVE-2026-8037 (CVSS 9.8), a pre-authentication OS command-injection flaw in Progress Kemp LoadMaster, began drawing active exploitation attempts on 29 June, days after a public proof-of-concept landed. The bug sits in the appliance's API: unsanitized input to the “/accessv2” endpoint (an out-of-bounds heap read in a string-escaping routine) lets an unauthenticated attacker inject commands and run code as root. The same defect affects other Progress ADC products (ECS Connection Manager, ObjectScale Connection Manager and the MOVEit WAF). eSentire noted the attempts it saw failed, but with a working PoC circulating, successful exploitation is expected to follow. Apply Progress's fixed release now, restrict management/API access, and pull the appliance off any untrusted network. - The Hacker News / eSentire TRU - Exploitation attempts from 29 Jun 2026 — reported 1 Jul 2026

item.title: [Critical] Critical SimpleHelp RMM auth-bypass exploited to drop new stealer malware — the remote-support tool that reaches into managed networks
item.description: CISA added CVE-2026-48558, a CVSS 10.0 authentication-bypass flaw in the SimpleHelp remote monitoring and management (RMM) platform, to its KEV catalog on 29 June; the 2 July federal deadline has now lapsed while exploitation continues. On OIDC-configured servers SimpleHelp fails to verify identity-token signatures, so an unauthenticated attacker can forge a fully authenticated “Technician” session — and attackers are already using it to drop the TaskWeaver loader and the new cross-platform Djinn infostealer (Windows, macOS, Linux). Roughly 14,000 SimpleHelp servers are online, an estimated 1,000 directly vulnerable. RMM tools are how MSPs and IT teams reach across managed estates, so a compromised server is a pre-authenticated path into many downstream networks. Patch now, pull consoles off the public internet, rotate technician credentials and OIDC secrets, and hunt RMM-connected endpoints for TaskWeaver/Djinn. - CISA KEV / BleepingComputer - KEV-added 29 Jun 2026 — deadline 2 Jul 2026 (lapsed); exploitation ongoing

item.title: [Critical] Splunk Enterprise flaw actively exploited — CISA tells federal agencies to patch by Sunday
item.description: CISA urged federal agencies to secure their systems against a critical Splunk Enterprise vulnerability, CVE-2026-20253, that is being exploited in attacks. The flaw affects Splunk Enterprise versions 10.2.0–10.2.3 and 10.0.0–10.0.6 and lets a remote attacker create or truncate arbitrary files via a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint — a primitive that can lead to system compromise. Splunk is a security and observability backbone in many enterprises, so a compromise both undermines detection and hands attackers a privileged pivot. Apply Splunk's fixed release on the accelerated timeline, restrict access to the affected endpoint, and review Splunk hosts for unexpected file changes. - BleepingComputer / CISA - Reported early Jul 2026

item.title: [High] New “CitrixBleed-pattern” NetScaler flaw exploited within 24 hours of disclosure
item.description: Citrix shipped fixes for six NetScaler ADC / NetScaler Gateway vulnerabilities, and the headline one — CVE-2026-8451 (CVSS 8.8), an insufficient-input-validation bug causing a memory overread in the appliance's SAML handling — was exploited in the wild less than 24 hours after public disclosure. Researchers at watchTowr showed that a malformed SAML request padded with whitespace forces the parser to read past its buffer and return adjacent process memory, echoing the CitrixBleed flaws whose leaked session tokens fueled major 2023–24 intrusions; honeypots observed live attempts from 30 June. Exposure requires the appliance to be configured as a SAML identity provider. Apply the fixed builds now, confirm which appliances use SAML, terminate active sessions and rotate credentials after patching, and watch authentication logs for anomalous SAML requests. - SecurityWeek / watchTowr - Patched late Jun 2026 — exploitation from 30 Jun; reported 1–2 Jul 2026

item.title: [High] Cisco confirms exploitation of a Unified Communications Manager SSRF flaw
item.description: Cisco confirmed that a high-severity server-side request forgery vulnerability, CVE-2026-20230, in Cisco Unified Communications Manager (Unified CM) is now being exploited in attacks. Unified CM underpins enterprise voice and collaboration and typically sits deep in the corporate network, so an SSRF that lets an attacker coerce server-side requests can enable internal reconnaissance and pivoting toward otherwise unreachable services. Apply Cisco's fixed release, restrict management-interface access, and review Unified CM logs for anomalous outbound requests. - BleepingComputer / Cisco - Exploitation confirmed — reported early Jul 2026

item.title: [High] “BlueHammer”: ransomware gangs now exploit a Microsoft Defender privilege-escalation flaw
item.description: Ransomware gangs are now exploiting a Microsoft Defender privilege-escalation vulnerability dubbed BlueHammer, tracked as CVE-2026-33825. The flaw was leaked by a security researcher in early April along with proof-of-concept exploit code, and it has since been folded into ransomware playbooks and added to CISA's KEV catalog. Because it abuses a component present on essentially every Windows endpoint, it is an attractive local escalation step after initial access. Apply the Microsoft update across the estate, prioritize internet-adjacent and high-value systems, and hunt for the known PoC behavior and unexpected Defender-related privilege changes. - BleepingComputer / CISA - PoC leaked early Apr 2026 — ransomware exploitation reported since

item.title: [Policy] Senate bill would force cybersecurity review — and possible recall — of Chinese-made networked medical devices
item.description: Senator Tom Cotton introduced the Countering Chinese Cyberthreats for Patients (“Countering CCP”) Act, which would direct the FDA and CISA to retroactively review the cybersecurity of Chinese-made networked medical devices already deployed in U.S. healthcare. Manufacturers would have to disclose the software in their devices, their development processes and server locations; regulators would verify that U.S. patient data is not stored on or transmitted through China-based servers; and HHS could halt distribution of risky devices — with recall for vendors that fail to provide the required information within three months. The bill follows the FDA's earlier warning that Contec CMS8000 monitors (relabeled as Epsimed MN-120) shipped with a backdoor. For IT and security leaders it is another marker of where supply-chain scrutiny of foreign-made connected devices is heading — SBOM-style disclosure, data-flow verification and recall authority. No action required yet; it is proposed legislation, not law. - U.S. Senate / Industrial Cyber - Introduced — reported 1 Jul 2026 (proposed, not enacted)
